This paper extends and builds upon the results of an earlier paper, in which we described how to use the tools of geometrical engineering to deform geometrically-engineered grand unified models into ones with lower symmetry. This top-down unfolding has the advantage that the relative positions of singularities giving rise to the many `low energy' matter fields are related by only a few parameters which deform the geometry of the unified model. And because the relative positions of singularities are necessary to compute the superpotential, for example, this is a framework in which the arbitrariness of geometrically engineered models can be greatly reduced.   In our earlier paper, this picture was made concrete for the case of deforming the representations of an SU(5) model into their Standard Model content. In this paper we continue that discussion to show how a geometrically engineered 16 of SO(10) can be unfolded into the Standard Model, and how the three families of the Standard Model uniquely emerge from the unfolding of a single, isolated E8 singularity.

# Geometric Unfolding of Grand Unified Models

This paper extends earlier work on using geometrical engineering to deform grand unified models into models with lower symmetry. Building upon these foundations, we develop a systematic framework in which the rich structure of grand unified theories can be geometrically realized and subsequently broken down to phenomenologically viable configurations.

Central to our approach is a top-down unfolding procedure that relates the positions of singularities—the geometric structures responsible for generating low-energy matter fields—through only a few geometric deformation parameters. Rather than treating the location of each singularity as an independent input, this method organizes them within a unified geometric picture, revealing the deep interdependencies that govern their arrangement.

The significance of this organization becomes especially clear when computing physical quantities. Because singularity positions are required to determine observables such as the superpotential, this framework greatly reduces the arbitrariness that has traditionally plagued geometrically engineered models. By constraining these positions through a small set of deformation parameters, the theory gains predictive power and internal consistency that would otherwise be absent.

To illustrate the utility of this framework, we demonstrate explicitly how a geometrically engineered **16** of SO(10) can be unfolded into the Standard Model. This example shows, in concrete terms, how the unfolding procedure translates the symmetry content of a grand unified representation into the matter content and gauge structure of low-energy physics.

Most strikingly, we find that the three families of the Standard Model uniquely emerge from the unfolding of a single, isolated E₈ singularity. This result suggests that the observed generational structure of matter is not an arbitrary feature but rather a natural consequence of the underlying geometry, with the exceptional group E₈ providing a compelling organizing principle for the entire fermionic spectrum.

# Geometric Engineering of Standard Model Families from an E8 Singularity

## Abstract

This paper applies geometrical engineering tools to deform geometrically-engineered grand unified models into lower-symmetry theories. Extending prior work on SU(5), we demonstrate how a **16** of SO(10) unfolds into Standard Model content. Our key result shows that the three families of the Standard Model uniquely emerge from the unfolding of a single, isolated E8 singularity, significantly reducing the arbitrariness inherent in geometrically engineered models.

## Introduction

The realization of gauge theories through the geometry of compactification manifolds has provided one of the most fruitful bridges between string theory and phenomenology. In geometric engineering, gauge symmetries arise from singularities in the internal geometry, matter fields localize on curves where singularity types enhance, and Yukawa couplings emerge at points of further enhancement. This framework has proven especially powerful in the context of F-theory and its dual descriptions, where the ADE classification of singularities maps directly onto the structure of gauge groups and their representations.

Despite these successes, geometrically engineered models have long suffered from a persistent shortcoming: the *arbitrariness* in the choice of matter content. While the gauge group is fixed by the singularity type, the number of matter families and their particular embedding often remains a matter of construction, requiring additional input to reproduce the observed spectrum of the Standard Model. The three-family structure of nature, in particular, has typically been imposed by hand rather than derived from first principles.

In this work, we address this arbitrariness directly. Building upon the well-developed machinery for deforming grand unified geometries, we show how the *unfolding* of singularities—the controlled resolution and deformation of a singular geometry into constituents of lower symmetry—can be used to descend from unified theories to the Standard Model in a natural way.

## Deforming Grand Unified Models

The starting point of our analysis is the observation that grand unified theories are naturally encoded in higher-rank singularities. An SU(5) GUT arises from an $A_4$ singularity, SO(10) from a $D_5$ singularity, and the exceptional groups from their corresponding exceptional singularities. The breaking of these unified symmetries to the Standard Model gauge group $SU(3) \times SU(2) \times U(1)$ corresponds geometrically to the partial deformation of the singular fiber.

Prior work established how the SU(5) unified structure could be deformed into its Standard Model constituents. The **10** and **$\bar{5}$** representations of SU(5), localized on matter curves, decompose into the quark and lepton multiplets as the $A_4$ singularity is unfolded. This provided a concrete geometric dictionary for the transition from grand unification to observable physics.

We extend this program to SO(10). The spinorial **16** representation of SO(10) is especially compelling from a phenomenological standpoint: it accommodates a complete generation of Standard Model fermions—including the right-handed neutrino—within a single irreducible representation. Geometrically, the **16** is localized on a matter curve associated with the $D_5$ singularity. By applying the unfolding procedure to this configuration, we demonstrate explicitly how the **16** decomposes into the full Standard Model content of a single family:

$$\mathbf{16} \rightarrow Q \oplus u^c \oplus d^c \oplus L \oplus e^c \oplus \nu^c$$

Each of these components emerges on the appropriate descendant curves as the $D_5$ singularity is deformed toward the Standard Model configuration. The geometry thus faithfully reproduces the hypercharge assignments and the multiplet structure of a generation.

## The E8 Singularity and the Origin of Three Families

The central result of this paper concerns the origin of the *number* of families. Rather than treating each family as an independent input, we consider the maximal exceptional singularity, **E8**, as a unifying structure from which the entire matter content descends.

The $E_8$ singularity occupies a distinguished position in the ADE hierarchy: it is the largest of the exceptional singularities and encodes, through its subsequent deformations, an extraordinarily rich structure of matter curves and enhancement points. When a single, isolated $E_8$ singularity is unfolded, the pattern of descendant singularities and their associated matter representations is fully determined by the geometry—there is no residual freedom to adjust the outcome.

Our analysis shows that this unfolding yields precisely **three** copies of the Standard Model matter content. In other words, the three families of quarks and leptons observed in nature arise *uniquely* from the geometry of a single $E_8$ point. The multiplicity of generations is not imposed but is instead a rigid consequence of the branching structure of the exceptional singularity as it deforms.

This result is significant for two reasons. First, it provides a geometric explanation for one of the most enigmatic features of the Standard Model: the existence of exactly three generations. Second, and more broadly, it demonstrates that the arbitrariness traditionally associated with geometrically engineered models can be substantially reduced when the construction is anchored in a maximal singularity. By starting from $E_8$ and allowing the geometry to dictate the descent, the family content is fixed rather than chosen.

## Discussion and Conclusions

We have shown that the tools of geometric engineering, when applied to the deformation of grand unified singularities, provide a natural and economical route from unified symmetry to Standard Model physics. Extending earlier SU(5) results, we detailed the unfolding of the SO(10) spinor **16** into a complete Standard Model generation, confirming that the spinorial matter curve decomposes correctly under the descent to lower symmetry.

Most importantly, we demonstrated that the three-family structure of the Standard Model emerges uniquely from the unfolding of a single, isolated $E_8$ singularity. This uniqueness is the key to reducing the arbitrariness that has historically limited the predictive power of geometrically engineered models. The family number, rather than being an external assumption, becomes a determined output of the exceptional geometry.

These findings suggest several avenues for future investigation. The interplay between the $E_8$ unfolding and the structure of Yukawa couplings—localized at points of maximal enhancement—may shed light on the observed hierarchies of fermion masses and mixings. Furthermore, embedding this construction within a global compactification, with attention to flux data and moduli stabilization, would be necessary to promote these local results into a complete model of particle physics. We anticipate that the principle established here—that maximal singularities constrain the low-energy spectrum—will continue to serve as a guiding thread in the search for realistic string vacua.

# Geometric Engineering of the Standard Model from SO(10) via E8 Singularity Unfolding

## Abstract

We extend our previous construction of Standard Model gauge dynamics from geometrically engineered SU(5) singularities to the more unified framework of SO(10) and its embedding within E8. In this work, we demonstrate how the complete **16** spinor representation of SO(10)—naturally accommodating a single generation of Standard Model fermions plus a right-handed neutrino—emerges from the unfolding of codimension-two singularities in an elliptically fibered Calabi-Yau fourfold. By systematically resolving the E8 singularity through a chain of partial deformations, we trace the geometric origin of each irreducible Standard Model representation to specific components of the exceptional divisor structure, with the matter curves and their intersection points encoding the Yukawa couplings.

Building on the SU(5) analysis, we show that the SO(10) enhancement provides a more economical geometric realization of gauge coupling unification while naturally implementing the seesaw mechanism through the singlet directions available in the **16**. The breaking to the Standard Model gauge group $SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ is achieved through a combination of flux-induced monodromy and the introduction of $U(1)$ hypercharge flux, which simultaneously resolves the doublet-triplet splitting problem that obstructed the minimal SU(5) construction.

We provide an explicit dictionary relating the local geometry—the deformation moduli, resolution parameters, and intersection numbers—to the physical spectrum, including the number of chiral generations and the structure of the CKM and PMNS mixing matrices. Our results establish SO(10) singularity unfolding as a robust intermediate step in the geometric engineering program, bridging the phenomenologically successful features of grand unified theories with the exceptional structure of E8 that underlies compactifications of F-theory and heterotic string theory. We conclude by outlining the phenomenological implications for proton decay and neutrino masses, and discuss the prospects for realizing three complete generations within a globally consistent compactification.

# Abstract

We investigate the emergence of Standard Model matter content through the geometric engineering of exceptional gauge structures on singular Calabi-Yau compactifications. Working within the framework of M-theory on $G_2$-manifolds and F-theory on elliptically fibered fourfolds, we demonstrate how the controlled deformation of ADE and higher-codimension singularities provides a natural mechanism for breaking $E_8$ and $SO(10)$ gauge symmetries into the observed $SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ structure. We show that matter representations localize at points of enhanced singularity, where the intersection of degeneration loci encodes chiral fermion content through the local geometry of vanishing cycles. In particular, we analyze how the unfolding of an $E_8$ singularity along a partial resolution flow sequentially descends through $E_6$ and $SO(10)$ subalgebras, with each deformation parameter corresponding to a geometric modulus controlling symmetry-breaking scales. The complete three-generation spectrum, including the $\mathbf{16}$ of $SO(10)$ decomposing into quarks, leptons, and right-handed neutrinos, arises from the resolution of codimension-three singular fibers whose monodromy structure we classify explicitly. We further examine the role of flux quantization and $G_4$-background data in fixing Yukawa couplings at points of maximal enhancement, and comment on the appearance of exotic states as obstructions to smooth deformation. Our results suggest that the hierarchical structure of Standard Model matter reflects an underlying geometric organization of singularities, providing a unified perspective in which gauge symmetry, matter content, and coupling structure emerge from a single deformation-theoretic principle. We conclude by discussing implications for moduli stabilization and the landscape of geometrically consistent vacua.
